lines.en: I sweep my broad tail over the seagrass.

lines.zh: 海草床很浅，我贴着底游。
lines.en: The grass bed is shallow; I hug the bottom.
I am heavy; I must turn well in advance.
Full of grass, my body rides even lower.
Do not follow too close; my tail is long.
I drift along like a floating log.
Seagrass slides over my broad back.
Seagrass brushes along my belly.
Thirty-two hearts; a bump will not break me.
I travel along the edge of the grass bed.
The current carries all this heavy flesh.
I lower my snout and push the blades aside.
A companion leads; I follow its wake.

lines.zh: 草床够宽，我可以慢慢逛。
lines.en: This meadow is wide; I take my time.

lines.zh: 我慢慢地拐过珊瑚，不碰它。
lines.en: I turn slowly past the coral without touching it.

lines.zh: 一群小鱼让开路，我照旧游。
lines.en: A shoal of small fish parts, and I keep going.

lines.zh: 我把鼻子探进沙里，找嫩草。
lines.en: I push my snout into the sand to find tender grass.

lines.zh: 水面就在头顶，我不急着上去。
lines.en: The surface is right above me. I am in no rush.
I float and watch the grass blades sway.
The sound of my chewing is soft.
The seagrass bed is quiet as an empty room.
I yawn, and water rushes into my mouth.
A layer of fine sand settled on my back.
I remember the taste of every patch here.
I breathe slowly, one breath lasting long.
Little fish dart beneath my belly.
Doing nothing at all suits me fine.
Sunlight comes through the water onto my back.
I push my nose above the surface.
The water hums low, like a lullaby.
This stone is one I often lean on.
Getting old; I rest after a short swim.
You stand out, standing on the grass bed.
Are you here to eat seagrass too?
I am this large; do I frighten you?

lines.zh: 你的船从上面划过去了。
lines.en: Your boat just slid past above us.
My eyes are small; I cannot see well.
The grass under your feet is my dinner.
Put the harpoon away; I do not bite.
Your skin looks a bit like mine.
I came up just to look at you.
Back away slowly; do not crush the grass.
Even this thick hide can hurt.
I was only eating grass.
The wound is deep along my ribs.
I sink into the grass to hide.
Thick hide, but that one knocked the air out.
I am old; I heal slowly now.
The hide is split; the flesh shows.
I do not want to fight; I want to leave.
I let out one long, low call.
The meadow sways; it is my head spinning.
That bundle of grass smells good.
Is that seagrass in your hand?
I smell tender leaves on the current.
That patch of seagrass smells tender.
I am not picky; grass will do.
My stomach growls louder than the water.
Wave it once and I will come over.
I know that tenderness by scent alone.
I approach slowly so I will not scare you.
Seagrass smells better than anything else.
Bump into me and you will bounce off.
Am I this big that I block your way?
Easy; my ribs are thick enough already.
You have scattered the current around me.
I shift aside so you can pass.
My leathery hide does not mind a knock.
You touched my tail just now.
Let us each give the other some room.
This grass bed is getting crowded.
After the bump I still swim slowly.
A mate arrives; I answer with a low call.
We graze side by side in the meadow.
This meadow is big enough for a calf.
Keep your distance; we are busy.
I touch her back gently with my snout.
The scent of my own kind calms me.
The water is warm this season, just right.
She swims with more ease than I do.
Our calf will follow us soon enough.
We circle the seagrass bed slowly.
Something down there is catching the light.
I pick it up to have a look.
It is not grass; it is hard.
I balance it up on my back.
Can this thing be eaten?
I hold it a while, then let it drop.
Anything heavy on the bottom interests me.
Do not grab it; I saw it first.
With a full mouth I cannot chew grass.
I push it along as I move.
That patch of grass looks the tenderest.
I have settled on this very patch.
The nearby grass has all been eaten.
I make my way over, in no hurry.
There is more grass behind that rock.
I smell something sweet over that way.
Fresh shoots grow at the meadow's far end.

lines.zh: 这条路线我走过很多次。
lines.en: I have taken this route many times.
My belly is empty; I must find food.
I swim toward the greenest water.
Almost there; a few more strokes.
The blades wave at me in the current.
I lower my head and move in slowly.
This patch will last me half a day.
Do not block me; I am here to graze.
The edge of the meadow is just ahead.
I smell soil and young leaves together.
I swim slowly, but my heading is right.
The grass moves; it is only the current.
Turning is hard work at my size.
I bite grass, not people.
I bump you only to ask for room.
This mouth of mine only chews seagrass.
Do not make me sweep my tail at you.
I push you so you do not crush the grass.

lines.zh: 三十二条命，不是用来打的。
lines.en: Thirty-two hearts were not meant for fighting.
I bite off a whole mouthful of grass.

lines.zh: 我慢慢顶开挡路的东西。
lines.en: I nudge the obstacle slowly out of my way.
Brawling in a grass bed is pointless.
I turn away and leave the fight alone.
I settle down into the seagrass bed.
A companion floats two strokes away.
The grass here is thick and the water clear.
I was already heavy when I was born.
Waves push sand up against my flippers.
I woke up and ate a meal first.
The smell of this meadow is familiar.
This shallow sea has room for me.
I sink slowly down onto the grass.
One large shadow rises from the bottom.
The surface burns; I sink lower.
Waves threw me ashore; I am too heavy.
I strain to lift my nose for air.
The blast rings underwater; my ears ache.
A fishing spear is stuck in my back.
This strange light makes my hide tighten.
The seagrass meadow has been stripped bare.
Lightning strikes the shallows; I freeze.
Below there is no grass, only emptiness.
